Digital Twin-Driven Generative Design of Multi-Layer Cultivation Systems for Vertical Farming with Solar Light
candidates.abstract: Multi-layer Cultivation Systems (MCSs) intensify urban food production. Designing MCSs for Vertical Farming with Solar Light (VFSL) delivers energy-saving benefits but is constrained by inter-layer shading, which limits productivity and conflicts with yield requirements. Therefore, optimal conceptual design is crucial. To address how to ensure complex designs meet stakeholder requirements during conceptual design, this study proposes a Digital Twin-driven Generative Design (DTGD) framework. The framework links stakeholder requirements with system architecture, fully incorporating theories related to system architecture, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), The Double Diamond (TDD), and Digital twin (DT). Using Digital Twin Modeling (DTM) and Candidate Architecture Decision (CAD) as core methods, it supports the generation and trade-off analysis of multiple Candidate Architectures (CAs). When applied to the design of MCSs in a case study, two CAs (square and zigzag cultivation) are generated. Within a design-stage DT model (an early-stage DT) for light simulation, key A-Frame design variables, including A-Frame Width (FW), A-Frame Height (FH), and the vertical height difference between adjacent planting containers (PCVH), are optimized to identify the optimal design solution. Cultivation experiments using the designed MCSs in a greenhouse in Handan, China, confirmed normal growth of cream lettuce in a single cycle. Based on this empirical data, the estimated annual production potential reaches 49.78 kg·m⁻²·year⁻¹ (assuming ten annual cropping cycles), satisfying the stakeholder yield requirement. This demonstrates the framework's practical feasibility for the evaluated case. Future work may incorporate Large Language Models to enhance automated design generation and explore alternative MCSs for wider urban adoption.

candidates.title: VibeFlow: An intelligent CFD workflow framework based on unified source-of-truth and dynamic parameter heuristics
candidates.abstract: This paper presents VibeFlow, an intelligent workflow framework for managing the complete lifecycle of computational fluid dynamics research. At its core, VibeFlow introduces a centralized case definition file, caseDict, serving as the single source of truth for every project stage. It persistently stores user objectives, physical assumptions, geometric parameters, mesh requirements, numerical configurations, post-processing evidence, and report conclusions, ensuring all decisions and artifacts remain traceable. Built upon this unified foundation, VibeFlow integrates two complementary operational modes within a single agent-based harness. The usage mode guides a case from initial requirement elicitation through parametric geometry construction, mesh generation, numerical simulation, post-processing, and final report compilation. The development mode supports creating, compiling, and validating user-defined functions, solver extensions, boundary conditions, and post-processing utilities, enabling seamless transition from code development to case execution. To address the inherent incompleteness of natural language requirements, VibeFlow incorporates a dynamic parameter heuristic that intelligently prioritizes missing parameters exerting the strongest influence on simulation outcomes, carrying the greatest physical risk, and lacking adequate evidence, thereby reducing unnecessary user interaction while safeguarding physical fidelity. Stage gating mechanisms enforce rigorous checkpoints assessing whether accumulated evidence meets minimum requirements before advancing to subsequent phases. On 315 benchmark cases, GPT-5.5 achieves 99.4% execution success and 99.4% physical fidelity. A complex SUBOFF submarine case confirms the framework’s ability to orchestrate the full workflow, from model development and validation through geometry, meshing, parallel computation, and reporting. These results demonstrate that VibeFlow advances CFD automation toward a reproducible, auditable, and human-collaborative research paradigm, with further details and resources available at vibeflow.org.cn

candidates.title: Mesh2Shell Neural Operator for Inverse Shape Optimization
candidates.abstract: Physics-driven design seeks high-performing geometries, which need not conform to a learned shape category. Parametric and latent-space approaches facilitate surrogate-based optimization, but restrict deformations to prescribed shape families or learned decoders. We introduce the Mesh-to-Shell Neural Operator (M2S-NO) as the mesh-to-shell component of a category-agnostic inverse shape optimization framework. We separate the explicit mesh used for design from the volumetric representation used for physics prediction. M2S-NO maps oriented surface samples to a surface-centered shell representation, such as TruncatedSDF or HeatSDF. A separate problem-specific PDE neural operator (PDE-NO) maps this representation to physical fields. Objective gradients update mesh vertices through both operators, without a latent shape decoder. Preconditioning and remeshing support free-form deformation, while fixed interfaces are controlled directly on the mesh. Optional shell-space proposals enable topology changes. We evaluate geometric matching, jet-engine brackets, and neutron moderators, with independent FEM and OpenMC evaluation. Relative to the best training designs, M2S-NO reduces maximum bracket displacement by 14.3% and increases neutron-sensor current by 13.8%. Optimization also succeeds from an out-of-distribution bracket initialization, demonstrating the framework's geometric flexibility.

candidates.title: Composable CAD: Sketch-to-CAD Program Synthesis in Parts
candidates.abstract: Designers often build CAD models part by part, and may iterate on individual components throughout the design process. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can synthesize CAD programs from sketches, but generating parts independently does not ensure that they are composable: components may lose the intended proportions and alignments or fail to join correctly where they meet. We present Composable CAD, a framework that uses off-the-shelf VLMs to synthesize a design space of independently sampled, interchangeable component programs, where any selection composes into a coherent CAD model. We recover design constraints from the sketch and use them to construct a coarse proxy that establishes how the components are sized, aligned, and attached. We then generate each component independently from its proxy and apply a deterministic rewrite to ensure that neighboring components meet at their prescribed interfaces. We evaluate Composable CAD across a range of objects and sketch styles and conduct two user studies. Compared to VLM-only baselines, our method produces more detailed, composable designs.

candidates.title: Inverse design of architectural floorplans with gradient-based optimization of binary subdivision graphs
candidates.abstract: Computer-aided floorplan synthesis automates a core task in architecture and construction planning: balancing room programs, connectivity, areas, and boundary constraints. The fuzzy nature of machine-learning models makes it difficult for generative methods to achieve the precision and predictable edits needed in architectural design. Building on a hypergraph representation coupling binary subdivision graphs with access graphs, this paper proposes a gradient-based inverse-design workflow for controllable floorplan synthesis. Its differentiable soft-split formulation converts subdivision parameters into continuous room masks, allowing room areas and compactness to be optimized while preserving a prescribed or retrieved subdivision structure. Compared with non-differentiable optimization, this method is faster and performs favorably on several connectivity metrics. Residential floorplan experiments show improved access satisfaction and area accuracy over existing methods. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated across several design scenarios, supporting interactive computer-aided design and controllable layout synthesis for early-stage decision making under varied design requirements.

candidates.title: CAD-WAM: Anticipating Geometry for Text-to-CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from text requires selecting operations that produce the intended changes to the geometry constructed so far. An incorrect operation can compromise subsequent steps, making reliable multi-step generation challenging. Existing methods based on large language models (LLMs) primarily learn to predict commands, without explicit supervision of the geometric states those commands should produce. Inspired by world-action models, we introduce CAD-WAM, which couples geometry-conditioned action generation with next-state prediction. We define complete modeling operations as actions in a CAD domain-specific language (DSL) and encode surface point clouds of intermediate solids into compact latent states using a pretrained variational autoencoder. An LLM backbone generates the next action from the target description and current geometric state, while an auxiliary head on the same backbone predicts the next state to provide geometric supervision during training. We construct step-wise training trajectories from parametric CAD models in the DeepCAD dataset, pairing each trajectory with an expert-level textual description. At inference, each generated action is executed by a CAD kernel, and the resulting solid is re-encoded to inform the next decision. On the DeepCAD test set, CAD-WAM outperforms the task-specific baselines in geometric accuracy and output validity, with larger gains on models requiring more operations, and produces more accurate geometry than general-purpose LLMs prompted with the same DSL. Ablations further show that next-state supervision reduces mean Chamfer distance by 13.2\% relative to an otherwise identical model trained only to predict actions. Code is available at https://github.com/Lzy-1037/CAD-WAM.

candidates.title: Research on Blended Teaching Reform of Engineering Drawing Course Empowered by AI Application on the BOPPPS Model
candidates.abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence technology, higher education is undergoing a profound transformation from the traditional "teacher-student" dual structure to a "teacher-AI-student" triadic structure.As a core course for logistics major, Engineering Drawing faces practical challenges such as insufficient student engagement due to the widespread use of AI tools.Based on the BOPPPS teaching model, this study takes the "Logistics Engineering CAD" course of the Logistics Management major at Shenzhen Technology University as an example, and constructs a blended teaching model with triadic collaboration among teachers, AI, and students.This paper elaborates on the role positioning and collaborative mechanisms of teachers, AI, and students in three stages-pre-class, in-class, and post-class-and demonstrates the implementation pathway of AI-empowered teaching through specific course chapters, providing a referable practical framework for the intelligent teaching reform of engineering practice-oriented courses.

candidates.title: Co-Construction of Production-Line AAS Geometric Models and Knowledge Graphs Driven by a Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Digital twin systems for a production line usually run on two models at once: an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) that holds asset information under IEC 63278, and a knowledge graph (KG) that records device topology and process semantics. On real projects, though, the two are built apart from each other. Engineers key the AAS geometric model in by hand from drawings and field measurements, while process engineers author the KG separately. The same data therefore gets entered twice, reuse is poor, and sooner or later the two models disagree. This paper presents a co-construction method that removes the duplication at its source. A fine-tuned vision-language model (VLM) reads the engineering sources a line already has, namely 2D/3D CAD drawings, on-site laser point clouds, and equipment technical manuals, and fills a standardized AAS; the KG is then derived from that AAS by fixed rules, so both models share one source. The method is arranged in four layers: multi-source data preprocessing with coarse-to-fine ICP spatial registration; LoRA-based domain adaptation of an open-source VLM supported by industrial prompt templates; automatic population of the AAS geometric, property, and connectivity submodels with conformance-checked .aasx generation on Eclipse BaSyx, plus QEM-based mesh simplification; and same-source KG derivation through fixed field-to-triple mapping rules, backed by a single-source constraint, automatic reconciliation, and incremental refresh with version traceability. We demonstrate the complete pipeline on a photovoltaic cell production line, and a parameterized Monte Carlo simulation of data consistency shows that, for manual single-entry error rates between 1% and 10%, conventional dual-entry modeling produces 4–39 times more data inconsistencies than the proposed single-source derivation, with the gap widening as the error rate grows. The method offers a reusable and extensible path toward production-line digital twin modeling; empirical validation on a physical line is planned as future work.

candidates.title: Automation of Tunnel Support Detailing with AI-Assisted Programming
candidates.abstract: Drafting tasks in geological engineering are time-consuming and often highly repetitive, with tunnel support drawings being a representative example. Although such tasks may appear straightforward and intuitive to experienced engineers, translating drafting logic into executable code typically requires substantial software development effort. While modern CAD and BIM platforms provide programming and automation capabilities, their effective use has traditionally depended on skilled programmers rather than domain engineers. This paper presents a practical case study in which a geological engineer with only basic programming experience leveraged recent advances in artificial intelligence, specifically large language models, to develop a custom code for automating tunnel support drawings. The workflow generates detailed support layouts directly from the tunnel contour and a limited set of user-defined engineering parameters, such as bolt spacing, liner thickness, and support class. Crucially, the approach preserves engineering judgement by requiring the engineer to define all design parameters and to review the final outputs, while automating repetitive drafting operations. The results demonstrate a viable pathway for lowering the barrier to engineering automation. The proposed approach is readily extendable to similar repetitive drawing tasks across a broad range of geological engineering applications.

candidates.title: Single-Image 3D Mesh Reconstruction via Point-Aware Diffusion (SPAR3D) and Bezier Spline Vectorization (SVG/EPS/DXF) for Engineering and Industrial Design Education
candidates.abstract: Abstract (ERIC 5-Element Standard): The purpose of this study is to evaluate browser-based single-image three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction and raster-to-vector contour tracing for computer-aided design (CAD), rapid prototyping, and additive manufacturing instruction. The methodology examines Stable Point-Aware 3D (SPAR3D) architecture—which couples point-cloud diffusion sampling with triplane mesh reconstruction—across 50 object categories (DS-3), alongside cubic Bezier spline quantization into Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), Encapsulated PostScript (EPS), and Drawing Exchange Format (DXF) for computer numerical control (CNC) laser cutting. Results demonstrate that SPAR3D reconstructs watertight textured 3D meshes averaging 42,500 to 61,500 vertices in a mean inference time of 6.20 seconds directly in a web browser, while vector tracing reduces geometric contour error below 0.42 pixels. By offloading neural point-cloud generation from local workstations to browser endpoints, vocational and engineering programs eliminate the requirement for 24-gigabyte VRAM GPUs. Implications for STEM and CTE curricula include accessible 2D-to-3D fabrication workflows. Additional materials include 6 tables, 34 references, CAD lab protocols, and 190 embedded URI links. candidates.title: CardioHolisticAI for multimodal deep learning based coronary artery disease risk stratification and personalized treatment recommendation
candidates.abstract: Despite the significant reduction in mortality and morbidity caused by coronary artery disease (CAD), early stratification of risk is important for timely intervention and individualised care. Most current CAD prediction methods rely on clinical variables, focus on single-modality analysis or simple fusion, and lack interpretability, calibration, and robustness assessment. The authors introduce CardioHolisticAI, a multimodal deep learning framework that also features MultiRiskNet for CAD risk stratification in Low, Medium, and High risk. MultiRiskNet leverages modality-specific encoders and attention-guided fusion to combine clinical features, modality-agnostic radiomic descriptors, and genomic pathway information while maintaining modality-specific representations. A multilevel explainability module integrates SHAP-based global importance, Integrated Gradients-based local attribution, radiomic feature ranking, and pathway-level genomic analysis. MultiRiskNet was evaluated with repeated five-fold cross-validation and achieved an accuracy of 98.50 ± 0.16%, a Macro-F1 score of 0.985 ± 0.0015, and a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.992 ± 0.0009, outperforming all evaluated unimodal and conventional fusion baselines. Noise injection, feature masking, and repeated-initialisation experiments suggest stable performance under the assessed internal conditions, and calibration analysis examined the reliability of the predicted probabilities. This is because the imaging source is non-cardiac and the source modalities are independent and not clinically validated at the patient level. Before clinical deployment, external evaluation in a patient-linked multimodal cardiac cohort is needed. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence support in synchronous collaborative CAD activities: task-dependent effects and methodological implications
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study explores the task-dependent effects of ChatGPT support in synchronous collaborative Computer-Aided Design (CAD) activities. While large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT are increasingly being integrated into engineering design, evidence on their influence in collaborative CAD activities remains limited. Addressing this gap, a between-subjects experiment was conducted with 22 pairs of engineering students performing three synchronous collaborative CAD tasks requiring varying combinations of CAD and domain-specific knowledge. To assess the task-dependent effects, the study evaluated taskwork through the number of CAD user actions, productivity, efficiency and CAD dominance. Results show that ChatGPT’s influence was highly task-dependent. In tasks relying primarily on CAD knowledge, ChatGPT-supported pairs exhibited lower productivity and efficiency. Conversely, in tasks requiring domain-specific engineering knowledge, ChatGPT support showed potential to improve efficiency. The study also offers methodological insights for designing controlled experiments involving ChatGPT support in collaborative CAD, underscoring that effective integration depends on task, tool and user-related factors. The findings further imply that integrating ChatGPT into engineering design education and practice requires developing competencies for critical and coordinated ChatGPT use within collaborative workflows, ensuring that ChatGPT complements rather than replaces designers. Future research should examine professional settings, teamwork and long-term adaptation to ChatGPT-supported synchronous collaborative CAD activities.

candidates.title: Impact of super resolution deep learning reconstruction with a 1024 matrix on CAD-RADS classification of intermediate coronary stenosis: A bicentric retrospective study
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Moderate coronary stenosis (CAD-RADS 3) is a diagnostic gray zone in coronary CT angiography (CCTA). We evaluated whether super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR), particularly with a 1024 matrix, modifies CAD-RADS classification and inter-reader agreement. Materials and methods: Thirty-nine CCTA examinations from two centers, each containing at least one 50-69% stenosis identified on the routine normal-resolution deep learning reconstruction (NR-DLR), were reconstructed with NR-DLR and SR-DLR (512 and 1024 matrices). Five experienced readers blindly assigned CAD-RADS categories. Agreement was assessed with Gwet's AC2 and paired reclassification with exact McNemar tests. Subgroup analyses (plaque composition, initial image quality) were exploratory. Results: Forty-six lesions were analyzed (19 calcified, 16 mixed, 10 non-calcified, one in-stent). Agreement remained excellent (AC2 0.89 [0.86-0.92], 0.87 [0.83-0.90] and 0.84 [0.81-0.88] for NR-DLR, SR-DLR-512 and SR-DLR-1024). Consensus CAD-RADS 2 rose from 6.5% to 21.7% with SR-DLR-1024 (p = 0.016; 10 lesions downgraded, 2 upgraded), predominantly in lesions with non-calcified components. Per-reader CAD-RADS 2 rates ranged from 13% to 30%, increasing significantly for two of five readers (p = 0.004). Conclusion: SR-DLR-1024 modified CAD-RADS classification in about one fifth of intermediate lesions while preserving excellent agreement. Without an invasive reference standard, these reclassifications reflect a change in reader interpretation rather than a proven gain in accuracy.

candidates.title: EL-RAKHAWI UNIFIED FRAMEWORK FOR SOVEREIGN AEROSPACE AND ADVANCED MANUFACTURING (US-AAM) A Revolutionary Architecture for Generative Topological Design, AI-Guided Non-Traditional Machining, Aero-Thermo-Energy Integration, and Self-Healing Supply Chain Operations

Unified efficiency equation E_aero_total = [(AI_opt · M_machinability) × (η_aero · Φ_renewable) × T_supply_chain] · (1 - Λ_waste) ensures strict dimensionless homogeneity preventing theoretical negative efficiency. Supply chain resilience P_continuity = 1 - ∏(1 - R_i · S_i) converts serial fragility to parallel redundancy. candidates.title: Subtractive Trajectory Generative Modeling: A Material-Removal-Centric Framework for Three-Dimensional Shape Generation
candidates.abstract: Three-dimensional shape generation has been studied through a variety of representations and learning paradigms, including voxel-based generation, point-cloud synthesis, implicit neural representations, neural radiance fields, Gaussian-based scene representations, and procedural computer-aided design (CAD) generation. Despite their differences, many approaches primarily formulate generation as the direct synthesis or reconstruction of a target representation. This paper proposes Subtractive Trajectory Generative Modeling (STGM), a material-removal-centric framework that formulates three-dimensional shape generation as the progressive transformation of an initial stock into a target solid through a sequence of removal operations. Instead of generating the final geometry exclusively as a static representation, STGM models the evolving residual material state, the geometry of each removal region, the ordering of operations, and the compatibility of each operation with manufacturing constraints. The framework combines a geometric state representation, a conditional removal policy, differentiable or approximately differentiable geometric updates, and a multi-objective optimization procedure. Its objectives include target-shape fidelity, preservation of required material, operation complexity, accessibility, and estimated manufacturing cost. A hierarchical strategy is proposed to organize coarse removal, intermediate structural formation, and fine geometric refinement. The paper defines a formal problem, presents a reference algorithm, specifies a training objective, and develops an experimental protocol for evaluating geometric accuracy, trajectory quality, manufacturability, and computational efficiency. STGM is presented as a research hypothesis rather than an empirically validated method. Its potential contribution lies in integrating material-state evolution and removal-sequence optimization into a unified generative formulation, while its novelty and effectiveness require systematic comparison with existing CAD sequence generation, constructive solid geometry, machining-aware modeling, and shape-generation approaches.

candidates.title: Fidelity metric with 3D shape descriptor for digital twin standardization
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive framework for assessing Digital Twin (DTw) fidelity through multi-modal deep learning, evaluating the correspondence between physical manufactured components and their digital CAD specifications. Six diverse vision architectures CLIP-ViT-B/32, ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, MobileNet-V2, ResNet-50, and EfficientNet-B0 were systematically evaluated using complementary metrics: cosine similarity for visual pattern matching, Descriptor Distance Index (DDI) for embedding space discriminability, and 3D geometry scoring via symmetric chamfer distance. The methodology integrates three data modalities: high-resolution multi-view photography, structured light scanning point clouds, and CAD model specifications. CLIP-ViT-B/32 demonstrated superior overall performance with the highest fused verification score (0.7868), excelling in cross-modal visual understanding between physical images and CAD renders. ViT-B/32 and MobileNet-V2 exhibited exceptional embedding space robustness with remarkably low DDI scores (0.0056 and 0.0037 respectively), while maintaining competitive cosine similarity. All models except ResNet-50 achieved optimal performance at 96-pixel input resolution, indicating efficient feature extraction at moderate scales. The integrated verification framework, combining visual, geometric, and embedding metrics through weighted fusion (F = 0.4C + 0.3(1-D) + 0.3G), provides a comprehensive assessment methodology for digital twin validation. These findings demonstrate that model selection should be guided by application priorities: CLIP-ViT-B/32 for visual-semantic understanding, ViT architectures for embedding space robustness, and MobileNet-V2 for computationally constrained environments. The proposed multi-metric approach advances standardization of fidelity assessment in precision manufacturing and digital twin implementation.

candidates.title: EDA-Agent: A Multi-Agent AI System for RTL Verification, Circuit Debugging, and Semiconductor Design Automation -TCAD-2026-2322 (IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems)
candidates.abstract: Hardware verification and debugging traditionally consume over 70% of digital Integrated Circuit (IC) design cycles. Engineers spend thousands of hours manually parsing static timing reports, inspecting Value Change Dump (VCD) waveform traces, and writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA). EDA-Agent is an open-source, multi-agent AI platform designed to automate Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code analysis, functional testbench generation, waveform failure debugging, synthesis area estimation, and timing slack optimization. To overcome the hallucination risks of pure neural generation, EDA-Agent employs a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with strict deterministic boundaries: AST Static Analysis: A custom regex/AST parser deterministically evaluates design violations, such as latch inference conditions and blocking assignment race hazards. Trace-Based VCD Waveform Debugging: The system parses standard IEEE 1364 VCD files to build a temporal transition matrix, allowing the agent to back-track state transitions and map assertion failures directly to faulty source code lines. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): The system grounds its reasoning in an indexed database of IEEE 1800-2017 SystemVerilog standards, Yosys manuals, and OpenSTA documentation. Empirical evaluations of EDA-Agent demonstrate 100% unit test accuracy on core parsing components, 94.2% waveform-based bug localization accuracy, and a 37.5x acceleration in SystemVerilog testbench generation compared to manual human workflows.

candidates.title: Dual-graph computable knowledge engineering for CAD-to-CNC macro synthesis
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize G-code, but autonomous CAD-to-CNC macro-generation must preserve geometry, process constraints, variable roles, equations, loop bounds, coordinate mappings, and controller syntax. This paper presents a dual-graph computable knowledge engineering method in which typed knowledge objects are selected by a semantic relation graph and converted by a computational dependency graph into acyclic variable-expression-loop dependencies. A seven-layer Macro-Structured Parametric CNC Code (Macro-SPCC) schema and Macro-Program Intermediate Representation (MPIR) organize the evidence, while deterministic modules perform evaluation, geometric checking, and FANUC Macro B compilation. Across 12 tire-mold lettering-insert tasks from six DXF cases and two toolpath configurations, the method achieved 91.7% accuracy, 50.0 percentage points above Text-RAG, and a 100.0% compilation pass rate. VERICUT confirmed continuity, endpoint reachability, and safe retraction, demonstrating a traceable, computationally closed, and executable synthesis process.

candidates.title: Machine Learning Computer-Aided Design of Electronic Devices and Circuits
candidates.abstract: Abstract Driven by the miniaturization of single components, which has reached few nanometers, chips can nowadays accommodate hundreds of billions of transistors. As a result, modern nanoelectronics devices and systems are becoming extremely complex. To remain truly effective, computer-aided design (CAD) tools must evolve in parallel with these advancements, keeping pace with the increasing demands of scale and functionality. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has seen an incredible development in several areas. In nanoelectronics, ML is already offering promising technological solutions that improve performance and provide predictions across the entire electronic design stack. From material properties to quantum transport and circuit behavior, ML techniques are making simulation workflows much more efficient and flexible, leading to a new paradigm of CAD: Machine Learning Computer-Aided Design. This review examines the latest developments in computer simulations for assessing the performance of electronic systems and the types of models used across the different levels of abstraction. We also discuss the challenges that still need to be addressed, especially the need for physics-based ML models, and explore future directions toward generative machine learning frameworks tailored specifically for electronic system design.

candidates.title: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
candidates.abstract: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), recent studies have shown that final answers do not always depend on the generated rationales. In particular, LLMs may rely on query-specific shortcuts rather than the information provided by their reasoning steps. In this paper, we investigate whether context-aware decoding (CAD), an existing contrastive decoding method, can mitigate such shortcut behavior when applied to CoT reasoning. We study this application as Rationale Contrastive Decoding (RCD), which contrasts the next-token distributions conditioned on the query with and without its rationale, amplifying tokens whose likelihood increases due to the rationale. We provide a theoretical interpretation of this decoding rule via a KL-regularized reward-maximization objective. Experiments across five reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that RCD improves answer accuracy over standard CoT. Furthermore, intervention analyses using ground-truth and random rationales reveal that RCD increases the behavioral dependence of final answers on the rationale content. Our findings suggest that contrastive decoding offers a simple, training-free approach to mitigating query shortcuts.

candidates.title: Deterministic Spatial Synthesis: A Compiler Architecture for LLM-Driven CAD-to-Blueprint Translation in Synthetic Environment Infrastructure (SEI)
candidates.abstract: Generative Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently exhibit non-deterministic variances when generating spatial geometries, rendering them susceptible to structural hallucination in production CAD pipelines. This paper introduces Synthetic Environment Infrastructure (SEI)—a deterministic compiler architecture converting natural language parametric constraints into validated blueprints via Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), Domus Mare FEA hydro-envelopes (180 kN·m capacity), and Think Furniture joinery compilation.

candidates.abstract: Premessa Leonardo’s CAD non è una ricerca isolata. È un pannello del trittico Leonardo’s Spatial Grammar, insieme a Leonardo’s Rulers e a Leonardo’s Score: tre indagini nate separate, una sola grammatica metrico-modulare dello spazio. candidates.title: Generative AI for Mechanical Systems Design: A Systematic Review of Language-Driven, Diffusion-Based, and Physics-Informed Approaches — Protocol for a Two-Tier Systematic Map and In-Depth Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Protocol of a systematic review on generative artificial intelligence for the design of mechanical systems, components and structures (2021–2026). The review covers three paradigms: language-driven approaches (large language models, vision-language models, LLM agents, CAD-as-language models), diffusion-based approaches (denoising diffusion, latent diffusion, flow matching) and physics-informed generative approaches. It uses a two-tier design: (1) a systematic map of all eligible studies, coded by paradigm, design task, design stage, design representation and evaluation type; (2) an in-depth critical synthesis of a core set of studies that quantitatively evaluate the physical validity, constraint satisfaction or manufacturability of generated designs, selected with criteria fixed before full-text assessment. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Searches were run in Scopus and Web of Science on 20 October 2026; this registration was made after title/abstract screening and before full-text assessment and data extraction.

candidates.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
candidates.abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

candidates.title: COMPUTER AND ENGINEERING GRAPHICS IN TRANSITION THROUGH A BIBLIOMETRIC AND THEMATIC REVIEW OF DISTANCE EDUCATION RESEARCH
candidates.abstract: Distance learning is increasingly relevant in technical education, particularly in engineering and computer graphics. The integration of digital technologies enables the development of students’ spatial visualization and creative design skills essential for modern engineering practice. This review examines how distance education has transformed teaching and learning in these fields by analyzing global studies from 2014 to 2025. Although online delivery presents challenges in visualization and interactivity, advances such as computer-aided design (CAD), simulation-based environments, and virtual laboratories are helping to bridge these gaps. The review identifies diverse program types, ranging from foundational design graphics to advanced applications in artificial intelligence, data science, and augmented reality. Despite significant progress, limited empirical evidence exists on learning outcomes and engagement. Through bibliometric analysis, this study maps thematic trends and collaboration patterns, offering evidence-based insights to enhance the quality and accessibility of engineering graphics education in the digital era
